basis: The paragraph opens with the lemma 'Et fecit Deus bestias terrae juxta species suas et jumenta et omne reptile terrae in'. The printing marks neither chapter nor verse, so the extent is the lemma this paragraph opens with, placed by fitting the whole commentary as one non-decreasing walk through Genesis rather than by reading this paragraph alone.
date_basis: Bede's dedicatory letter to Acca of Hexham says the work was undertaken at Acca's asking and first carried only as far as Adam's expulsion from paradise, in two books, and was afterwards extended. Acca held Hexham from 709 to 731. The four-book redaction Migne prints is conventionally placed in the early 720s and the two-book one shortly before it; the range covers both, and no source held here narrows it. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1850 printing.
text: Et fecit Deus bestias terrae juxta species suas et jumenta et omne reptile terrae in genere suo. Notanda transmutatio verborum, quia supra dictum est, quod producere jusserit Deus terram, et jumenta, et reptilia, et bestias terrae; nunc autem, mutato ordine, fecisse dicitur Deus bestias terrae et jumenta et omne reptile terrae; et intelligendum quod dicto citius omne quod voluit fuit; nilque differt quod loquela humana prius in creaturarum ordine nominet, quas divina potentia condidit simul cunctas.
